state.objective: Investigate replacing repository /tests and its delegated test-policy dependencies with Can-authored tests. The user requires removal of host test harnesses, explicitly permits a test backend other than TypeScript, and requires arbitrary normal Can functions in tests. This round is design research, not implementation. Native compiler and platform mechanics are permitted; hiding old scenarios or expected-versus-actual decisions in native helpers is not.
state.frontend: The existing Go checker produces a checked Program with functions, entry regions, assertions, native declarations and specializations. Typed IR represents calls, closures and captures, invocation preparation, matching, completions, error propagation and coordination. Production and assertion entrypoints share the checked program and current TypeScript/Bun emission. The inspected compiler contains no runnable general Can interpreter.
state.semantics: A complete alternate executor must preserve arbitrary Can functions, bigint arithmetic, Object.is float identity, Bun.deepEquals-style structural and nominal equality, opaque/callable identities, closure capture, domain and standard error occurrences, fixture queues, raw exchanges, asynchronous coordination, ownership and resource lifetime. Actual and expected assertion expressions are executable IR regions, not merely literal data. This is substantially more than traversing a test-case table.
state.current_execution: Existing Go supervision runs bounded isolated Bun assertion workers, enforces deadlines and reaps processes. Its report protocol is assertion-specific, so it is reusable evidence for mechanics, not an existing live-suite implementation. Can process::run, files and JSON operations allow real effects in ordinary main; attached asserts intentionally reject live platform calls. No general finally exists, and an in-process timer cannot reliably preempt an infinite loop or guarantee cleanup after forced termination.
state.ownership: In every option, Can must author selection, fixtures, case sequence, suite scheduling policy, expectations, comparisons, verdicts and reporting policy. A native supervisor can enforce generic child lifetime, isolation, resource ceilings and report transport; Can receives abnormal exits/timeouts as facts and applies suite policy. An internal test-plan IR is acceptable metadata around full Can functions, but a restricted DSL, partial interpreter or silent host fallback violates the endpoint.
state.gaps: All choices still need a live-suite protocol, owned temporary workspaces, managed child descriptors/signals, browser automation and independent native/SQL observations. Those APIs must expose generic actions or facts, not prewritten test procedures or pass/fail answers. Existing browser::* is in-page DOM support rather than remote automation. No backend choice alone supplies these missing capabilities.
state.trust: Production compiler and runtime tests must compile and run candidate fixtures via the production TypeScript/Bun backend even if their coordinator runs elsewhere. A separate interpreter reduces shared execution machinery but still shares parser/checker/IR and is not an independent full oracle. A digest-identified known-good runner toolchain or executor can be kept distinct from the candidate. Preserve independent expected vectors, seeded failures and full/partial/blocked coverage evidence.
state.limits: There are no external users or compatibility obligations. The laptop has a 256 GB disk and tight load limits. No benchmarks or broad builds are allowed now; no speed or memory advantage has been measured. Bound jobs, time, output and storage; register cleanup immediately and reclaim inactive owned runs. Reuse builds within a run without persistent private bundles or copied dependency trees. The choice should minimize implementation and semantic-maintenance burden while meeting full Can semantics, coverage and isolation.

backend.instructions: Which execution architecture should be the starting recommendation for this migration, given unrestricted normal Can functions, Can-owned test decisions, full production coverage, and bounded implementation/resource cost? Select from supplied evidence; do not infer measured performance or assume unavailable APIs exist.

criteria.supervised_bun: Reuse full Can-to-TypeScript/Bun lowering for Can suite and helper bodies. Extend generic native supervision for bounded isolated workers and owned cleanup; keep all scenario, scheduling and verdict policy in Can. Identify the trusted suite toolchain separately from the candidate. Add missing observation APIs and protocol without introducing a second language runtime.
criteria.full_ir_interpreter: Implement a complete Go interpreter of checked Can IR for suite and helper functions, including language semantics and native/platform integration. Use external containment and a separately identified executor; keep policy in Can and still run subject fixtures through production TypeScript/Bun. Accept the cost of maintaining this additional full runtime to avoid compiling suite bodies to TypeScript.
criteria.native_codegen: Build a full additional Can code-generation backend and corresponding runtime/platform support for native suite executables. Preserve arbitrary helpers and Can-owned policy, supervise execution, record executor origin, and continue production TypeScript/Bun checks of subjects. Undertake this broader backend investment for testing.
criteria.undetermined: Do not yet prefer any offered backend; the supplied facts leave a material architecture question that must be answered by a focused investigation before selecting a starting direction.
